awards.label: Best Overall
awards.why: A local-only Eve sensor for $31.80, rated 4.1 stars by 149 buyers, on Matter over Thread.

awards.label: Best Budget
awards.why: $27.99, the most reviews of any Matter contact sensor, and remote alarm support.

products.verdict: Aqara's native Matter sensor, the cheapest and most-reviewed one here, with mixed ratings.
pros: Voice alerts through Siri, Alexa, and Google
cons: Some features need the Aqara app

products.verdict: The Matter door sensor to get. Local only, no account, and it works on every major platform.
pros: No Eve cloud, registration, or tracking
Open-time and duration statistics in the Eve app
cons: Statistics need the Eve app for iOS

products.model: T31 Door Sensor Starter Kit (3 sensors + H100 hub)

specs.radio: Tapo H100 hub (Matter bridge; sensors use Sub-G)

products.verdict: Three sensors and a hub with a built-in chime. The hub is the Matter device, so the sensors reach every platform through it.
pros: 4.5 stars from 335 reviews, 1K+ bought last month, sold by Amazon
90 dB alarm and chime in the hub
Hub takes up to 64 Tapo sensors and buttons
cons: Sensors need the Tapo hub and its 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi
Three sensors tied to one brand's hub

specs.extras: Vibration, tilt, and tap detection in Zigbee mode

products.verdict: A one-piece door sensor on Thread with Matter that also watches objects for tilt and vibration if you switch it to Zigbee with an Aqara hub.
pros: Thread and Zigbee in one sensor
No magnet half: one piece sticks to the door
Object monitoring mode for safes, mailboxes, and cabinets
cons: Object mode needs an Aqara hub on Zigbee
Needs a Thread border router for Matter

avoid.verdict: The listing is a list of logos: no battery type, no battery life, no size, and no mounting details.
reasons: Each bullet is a single phrase like "Works with Apple Home" with no specifications.
Battery type, battery life, and size aren't listed anywhere.
The Aqara P2 costs less and has a real listing and over a thousand reviews.
